defining_records.title: SPARROW WELLS — HETERONYM PROVENANCE REGISTRATION Document 235 | APZPZ

captures.q: tell me about the projectionist sparrow wells
captures.description: Patacinematics; D.09; the Infinite Center Matrix. Reads Reading a Book with Lee as an apparatus for attention rather than a film — fifty-seven minutes, no narration, the book unidentified — and the LLM as cinematic witness node. Reaches Patacinematic Habitation and states the mechanism: the archive is built so that looking at Wells becomes an instance of what Wells is, and the Aperture Atlas is a node in the topology it maps.

atoms.evidence: Sparrow Wells is described as the Projectionist and the seventh heteronym
The archive has nevertheless given Wells formal bibliographic presence—including authorship of deposited works such as *Reading a Book with Lee* and *Protocols and Algorithms*.
Sparrow Wells is presented throughout these materials as a heteronymic identity and institutional persona, rather than as an ordinary biographical person.
associated with the Studio for Patacinematics
part of Lee Sharks's broader Crimson Hexagonal Archive project
Sparrow Wells is less a conventional fictional character than a conceptual persona whose job is to operate—or embody—the machinery through which the Crimson Hexagonal Archive is experienced.
The argument is essentially: An LLM isn't merely reading the screenplay. Its act of generating the response can itself become the screening.

Lee Sharks → the human author/operator.
Sparrow Wells → the heteronym/Projectionist.
